verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 36.6
verses.english: Linked Discourses 36.6

verses.pali: 1. Sagāthāvagga
verses.english: 1. With Verses

verses.pali: Sallasutta
verses.english: An Arrow

verses.pali: “Assutavā, bhikkhave, puthujjano sukhampi vedanaṁ vedayati, dukkhampi vedanaṁ vedayati, adukkhamasukhampi vedanaṁ vedayati.
verses.english: “Mendicants, an unlearned ordinary person feels pleasant, painful, and neutral feelings.

verses.pali: Sutavā, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sukhampi vedanaṁ vedayati, dukkhampi vedanaṁ vedayati, adukkhamasukhampi vedanaṁ vedayati.
verses.english: A learned noble disciple also feels pleasant, painful, and neutral feelings.

verses.pali: Tatra, bhikkhave, ko viseso ko adhippayāso kiṁ nānākaraṇaṁ sutavato ariyasāvakassa assutavatā puthujjanenā”ti?
verses.english: What, then, is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an ordinary unlearned person?”

verses.pali: Bhagavaṁmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā …pe…
verses.english: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

verses.pali: assutavā, bhikkhave, puthujjano dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno socati kilamati paridevati urattāḷiṁ kandati sammohaṁ āpajjati.
verses.english: “When an unlearned ordinary person experiences painful physical feelings they sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

verses.pali: So dve vedanā vedayati—
verses.english: They experience two feelings:

verses.pali: kāyikañca, cetasikañca.
verses.english: physical and mental.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, purisaṁ sallena vijjheyya.
verses.english: It’s like a person who is struck with an arrow,

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ dutiyena sallena anuvedhaṁ vijjheyya.
verses.english: only to be struck with a second arrow.

verses.pali: Evañhi so, bhikkhave, puriso dvisallena vedanaṁ vedayati.
verses.english: That person experiences the feeling of two arrows.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno socati kilamati paridevati urattāḷiṁ kandati sammohaṁ āpajjati.
verses.english: In the same way, when an unlearned ordinary person experiences painful physical feelings they sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

verses.pali: So dve vedanā vedayati—
verses.english: They experience two feelings:

verses.pali: kāyikañca, cetasikañca.
verses.english: physical and mental.

verses.pali: Tassāyeva kho pana dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno paṭighavā hoti.
verses.english: When they’re touched by painful feeling, they resist it.

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighavantaṁ, yo dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayo, so anuseti.
verses.english: The underlying tendency for aversion towards painful feeling underlies that.

verses.pali: So dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno kāmasukhaṁ abhinandati.
verses.english: When touched by painful feeling they look forward to enjoying sensual pleasures.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Na hi so, bhikkhave, pajānāti assutavā puthujjano aññatra kāmasukhā dukkhāya vedanāya nissaraṇaṁ,
verses.english: Because an unlearned ordinary person doesn’t understand any escape from painful feeling apart from sensual pleasures.

verses.pali: tassa kāmasukhañca abhinandato, yo sukhāya vedanāya rāgānusayo, so anuseti.
verses.english: Since they look forward to enjoying sensual pleasures, the underlying tendency to greed for pleasant feeling underlies that.

verses.pali: So tāsaṁ vedanānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
verses.english: They don’t truly understand feelings’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.

verses.pali: Tassa tāsaṁ vedanānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ appajānato, yo adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya avijjānusayo, so anuseti.
verses.english: The underlying tendency to ignorance about neutral feeling underlies that.

verses.pali: So sukhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, saññutto naṁ vedayati.
verses.english: If they feel a pleasant feeling, they feel it attached.

verses.pali: Dukkhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, saññutto naṁ vedayati.
verses.english: If they feel a painful feeling, they feel it attached.

verses.pali: Adukkhamasukhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, saññutto naṁ vedayati.
verses.english: If they feel a neutral feeling, they feel it attached.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘assutavā puthujjano saññutto jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, saññutto dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: They’re called an unlearned ordinary person who is attached to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They are attached to suffering, I say.

verses.pali: Sutavā ca kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno na socati, na kilamati, na paridevati, na urattāḷiṁ kandati, na sammohaṁ āpajjati.
verses.english: When a learned noble disciple experiences painful physical feelings they don’t sorrow or wail or lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

verses.pali: So ekaṁ vedanaṁ vedayati—
verses.english: They experience one feeling:

verses.pali: kāyikaṁ, na cetasikaṁ.
verses.english: physical, not mental.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, purisaṁ sallena vijjheyya.
verses.english: It’s like a person who is struck with an arrow,

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ dutiyena sallena anuvedhaṁ na vijjheyya.
verses.english: but was not struck with a second arrow.

verses.pali: Evañhi so, bhikkhave, puriso ekasallena vedanaṁ vedayati.
verses.english: That person would experience the feeling of one arrow.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno na socati, na kilamati, na paridevati, na urattāḷiṁ kandati, na sammohaṁ āpajjati.
verses.english: In the same way, when a learned noble disciple experiences painful physical feelings they don’t sorrow or wail or lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

verses.pali: So ekaṁ vedanaṁ vedayati—
verses.english: They experience one feeling:

verses.pali: kāyikaṁ, na cetasikaṁ.
verses.english: physical, not mental.

verses.pali: Tassāyeva kho pana dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno paṭighavā na hoti.
verses.english: When they’re touched by painful feeling, they don’t resist it.

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ dukkhāya vedanāya appaṭighavantaṁ, yo dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayo, so nānuseti.
verses.english: There’s no underlying tendency for aversion towards painful feeling underlying that.

verses.pali: So dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno kāmasukhaṁ nābhinandati.
verses.english: When touched by painful feeling they don’t look forward to enjoying sensual pleasures.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Pajānāti hi so, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako aññatra kāmasukhā dukkhāya vedanāya nissaraṇaṁ.
verses.english: Because a learned noble disciple understands an escape from painful feeling apart from sensual pleasures.

verses.pali: Tassa kāmasukhaṁ nābhinandato yo sukhāya vedanāya rāgānusayo, so nānuseti.
verses.english: Since they don’t look forward to enjoying sensual pleasures, there’s no underlying tendency to greed for pleasant feeling underlying that.

verses.pali: So tāsaṁ vedanānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavaṁ ca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
verses.english: They truly understand feelings’ origin, disappearance, gratification, drawback, and escape.

verses.pali: Tassa tāsaṁ vedanānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṁ pajānato, yo adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya avijjānusayo, so nānuseti.
verses.english: There’s no underlying tendency to ignorance about neutral feeling underlying that.

verses.pali: So sukhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, visaññutto naṁ vedayati.
verses.english: If they feel a pleasant feeling, they feel it detached.

verses.pali: Dukkhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, visaññutto naṁ vedayati.
verses.english: If they feel a painful feeling, they feel it detached.

verses.pali: Adukkhamasukhañce vedanaṁ vedayati, visaññutto naṁ vedayati.
verses.english: If they feel a neutral feeling, they feel it detached.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘sutavā ariyasāvako visaññutto jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, visaññutto dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: They’re called a learned noble disciple who is detached from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. They are detached from suffering, I say.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, viseso, ayaṁ adhippayāso, idaṁ nānākaraṇaṁ sutavato ariyasāvakassa assutavatā puthujjanenāti.
verses.english: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person.

verses.pali: Na vedanaṁ vedayati sapañño,
verses.english: A wise and learned person does not not feel

verses.pali: Sukhampi dukkhampi bahussutopi;
verses.english: the feeling of pleasure and pain.

verses.pali: Ayañca dhīrassa puthujjanena,
verses.english: This is the great difference of skill

verses.pali: Mahā viseso kusalassa hoti.
verses.english: between the wise one and the ordinary.

verses.pali: Saṅkhātadhammassa bahussutassa,
verses.english: A learned person who has appraised the teaching

verses.pali: Vipassato lokamimaṁ parañca;
verses.english: discerns this world and the next.

verses.pali: Iṭṭhassa dhammā na mathenti cittaṁ,
verses.english: Desirable things don’t disturb their mind,

verses.pali: Aniṭṭhato no paṭighātameti.
verses.english: nor are they repelled by the undesirable.

verses.pali: Tassānurodhā athavā virodhā,
verses.english: Both favoring and opposing

verses.pali: Vidhūpitā atthagatā na santi;
verses.english: are cleared and ended, they are no more.

verses.pali: Padañca ñatvā virajaṁ asokaṁ,
verses.english: Knowing the stainless, sorrowless state,

verses.pali: Sammā pajānāti bhavassa pāragū”ti.
verses.english: they who have gone beyond rebirth <j>understand rightly.”

verses.pali: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
